claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "The Space-Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality", series "Acquisition Threat Support", published 2010-03-30 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2009-12-01, DIA document number DIA-08-1003-016. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.

claims.text: Author of record per the DIA letter of 9 January 2018, item 25: "Space_Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality, Dr J Cramer, Univ of Washington."
The released cover page reads "30 March 2010 / ICOD: 1 December 2009 / DIA-08-1003-016," series "Acquisition Threat Support." The author line is redacted under (b)(6).

The earlier KLAS-TV list titles the same document "Quantum Entanglement Communication," stating the tasking directly: whether entanglement can be made to carry a signal, and what that would mean for space communication.
